s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of painless nodules with vesicles and hemorrhagic crusts on the fingers, with associated arm and forearm discomfort
salient_findings: Vesicles that ruptured and formed hemorrhagic crusts
Discomfort and pain along the medial aspect of the right arm and forearm
key_facts: 30-year-old male
Dairy farm worker
Multiple painless nodules on fingers of both hands
Nodules appeared 1 month prior to presentation
Vesicles developed 7-10 days after initial nodules
Hemorrhagic crusts formed after vesicle rupture
Discomfort and pain along the medial right arm and forearm
Denies trauma or insect bites
Cow had similar lesions on its teats
3-4 firm, non-tender nodules with central hemorrhagic crusts and surrounding erythema on proximal phalanges of both hands
Mild tenderness and increased warmth along the medial right arm and forearm

shortlist.label: Orf virus infection
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical presentation of painless nodules with vesicles and hemorrhagic crusts, and the patient's occupation as a dairy farm worker increases the likelihood of exposure to the virus

shortlist.label: Milker's nodule
shortlist.why_kept: Also known as paravaccinia, this condition is common in individuals who work with cattle and presents with similar symptoms to the patient's condition

shortlist.label: Paravaccinia virus infection
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to Orf virus infection, paravaccinia virus infection is a plausible diagnosis given the patient's symptoms and occupation

shortlist.label: Erysipeloid
shortlist.why_kept: This bacterial infection is common in individuals who work with animals and can cause skin lesions similar to the patient's condition

shortlist.label: Pseudocowpox
shortlist.why_kept: Also known as milker's nodule, pseudocowpox is a viral infection that can cause similar symptoms to the patient's condition and is a plausible diagnosis given the patient's occupation

raw.rationale: The patient's occupation as a dairy farm worker and the presence of similar lesions on the cow's teats, along with the characteristic clinical presentation of painless nodules evolving into vesicles and hemorrhagic crusts, are highly suggestive of Orf virus infection.

rejected.label: Milker's nodule
rejected.why: While milker's nodule is also an occupational disease of dairy workers, it is typically caused by Paravaccinia virus and presents differently.

rejected.label: Paravaccinia virus infection
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and the fact that the cow had similar lesions point more towards Orf virus infection.

rejected.label: Erysipeloid
rejected.why: Erysipeloid typically presents with a well-demarcated, erythematous lesion, often with a distinctive border, and is usually associated with handling infected animals or their products, but the description does not fully match the patient's presentation.

rejected.label: Pseudocowpox
rejected.why: Pseudocowpox (Milker's nodule) is caused by Paravaccinia virus and has a different clinical presentation compared to the one described.
